column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale
angkor-thom|9.6,9.7,9.7,9.5,9.3|-|Large Khmer royal city remains globally extraordinary, but Bayon and other sub-sites must not duplicate all ensemble depth.
koh-ker-archaeological-site|9.3,9.6,9.6,9.3,9.1|-|Important former Khmer capital with pyramid and dispersed temples; overall breadth lower than the Angkor World Heritage ensemble.
sambor-prei-kuk-temple-zone|9.2,9.6,9.6,9.2,9.1|-|Exceptional pre-Angkorian temple-city remains, but preservation and visit depth below Angkor's vast ceremonial landscape.
banteay-chhmar-temple|9.1,9.5,9.5,9.2,8.9|-|Great but more fragmented remote Khmer temple complex, not equal in visitor accessibility or depth to major Angkor temples.
preah-khan-kompong-svay|9.0,9.5,9.4,8.9,8.9|-|Huge historically interesting royal temple remains with sparse restoration; one site does not match citywide Angkor experience.
cardamom-mountains|9.3,9.5,9.3,8.9,9.1|-|Major tropical forest conservation region, but fragile habitat and difficult visitor access differ from a curated 9.5 sightseeing experience.
virachey-national-park|9.2,9.4,9.2,8.4,8.8|-|Ecologically significant remote forests; specialized limited tourism has less visitor accessibility and breadth than global flagship parks.
tonle-sap-lake|9.0,9.2,9.5,8.8,9.2|-|Outstanding flood-pulse lake and livelihoods, but individual shore excursions are less extraordinary than whole watershed ecology.
tonle-sap-biosphere-reserve|9.1,9.3,9.5,8.5,9.1|-|Wetland wildlife importance is exceptionally high; protection-area designation alone does not guarantee broad tourism discovery.
keo-seima-wildlife-sanctuary|9.1,9.3,9.2,8.4,8.7|-|Critical endangered-primate sanctuary; guided wildlife viewing cannot match the breadth of a national park visitor itinerary.
mekong-irrawaddy-dolphin-conservation-area|8.9,9.3,9.2,8.8,8.6|-|Rare freshwater cetacean habitat, but sightings and narrow boating route should not inherit the entire Mekong's overall score.
kampi-irrawaddy-dolphin-pool|8.6,9.1,8.8,8.7,7.4|-|Important dolphin observation pool, yet the brief single-site outing is a component of the wider conservation area.
phnom-kulen-national-park|9.0,9.3,9.4,9.0,8.9|-|High Khmer religious history and waterfall landscape, with restricted depth relative to the much larger Angkor complex.
beng-mealea|9.2,9.5,9.4,9.2,8.8|-|Dramatic overgrown sandstone temple, though one complex is not as historically singular as Angkor Wat itself.
roluos-temples|9.0,9.3,9.3,9.1,8.9|-|Significant early Khmer temple group, whose three main monuments offer less scope than central Angkor.
tuol-sleng-genocide-museum|9.1,9.4,9.9,9.0,8.9|-|Profound and irreplaceable historical testimony, with compact site experience distinct from the wider memorial-site UNESCO group.
choeung-ek-genocidal-center|9.0,9.4,9.8,8.8,8.3|-|Very significant genocide memorial, with intense but limited on-site discovery and shorter visit than a large museum.
cambodian-memorial-sites-unesco|9.2,9.5,9.9,8.9,9.0|-|Multi-location memorial heritage carries profound significance; scoring it as a visit must not add each component's full impact.
national-museum-cambodia|8.8,9.1,9.3,9.1,8.8|-|Major Khmer collection with cultural relevance, but less global collection breadth than National Palace Museum or National Museum of Korea.
koh-rong-island|8.9,9.1,8.3,9.1,8.8|-|Excellent tropical beaches and island nature, but recreational quality is not worldwide historic or ecological singularity.
koh-rong-samloem-island|8.7,9.0,8.2,9.0,8.6|-|Fine quieter island beach destination with fewer independently globally rare features than conservation-dominant islands.
angkor-wat-central-towers|9.1,9.5,9.7,9.1,7.8|-|Sacred center of Angkor Wat retains significance, but cannot inherit the entire temple's grounds and exploration depth.
prasat-thom-koh-ker|9.0,9.4,9.4,9.0,7.9|-|Unusual pyramid within Koh Ker, distinctly narrower visitor scope than the whole archaeological site.
baphuon-temple|8.9,9.2,9.3,9.1,8.0|-|Important pyramidal Khmer temple within Angkor Thom, not the full magnitude of the parent walled city.
terrace-of-the-elephants|8.6,9.0,9.1,8.8,7.5|-|Historic carved royal terrace, whose short monument visit has limited breadth within Angkor Thom.
pre-rup|8.8,9.2,9.2,8.9,7.9|-|Strong temple-mountain and sunset photography, but lower historic singularity and scope than the leading temples.
royal-palace-phnom-penh|8.8,8.9,9.1,9.0,8.7|-|Major modern royal architecture and grounds, yet not on the historical scale of the Forbidden City or Hofburg.
silver-pagoda|8.6,9.0,9.1,8.9,8.0|-|Treasured royal religious interior within palace, not a standalone multi-day monument.
kep-crab-market|7.8,7.9,7.3,8.6,7.2|-|Distinctive seafood market food experience is strong, while global historic uniqueness and visit depth are modest.

angkor-archaeological-park|10.0,10.0,10.0,9.8,10.0|-|Retain globally defining protected Khmer archaeological ensemble covering several capitals, temples, infrastructure and museums; individually permitted field-specific tens are supported by full historic urban scale. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/668

angkor-thom-south-gate|8.8,9.0,8.8,8.9,6.9|architecture=9.2,history=9.1|Outstanding sculpted causeway and well-preserved gate of Angkor Thom but a short entrance stop, not the complete walled capital; 9.5+ global uniqueness and depth are overstated. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/07/03/angkor-thom/

angkor-wat|10.0,10.0,10.0,9.8,9.5|-|Retain exact approved world-defining architecture/history/impact for extraordinary single Khmer temple and broad sacred grounds, distinguished from Angkor Archaeological Park itself. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/668

banteay-srei-temple|9.5,9.9,9.8,9.5,8.8|-|Retain globally distinctive pink-sandstone microcarving and 10th century Khmer art; although compact, outstanding sculptural refinement is genuinely unusual among Angkor monuments. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/04/banteay-srei/

bayon-temple|9.7,9.9,9.8,9.6,9.0|-|Retain world-class singular face towers, carved narrative reliefs and capital-city ritual significance; Bayon is a substantial temple complex, not merely one decorative gateway. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/05/bayon/

central-cardamom-national-park|8.9,9.1,8.9,8.6,8.9|-|Important tropical forest and biodiversity protection, with varied conservation landscapes; guided wilderness visit breadth should not automatically inherit all regional Cardamom Mountains ecology. Source: https://cambodia.conservation.org/projects/central-cardamom-mountains-landscape

mekong-flooded-forest|8.7,9.1,9.0,8.5,8.6|-|WWF documents ecologically exceptional riverine habitats and rare freshwater species, but a landscape-wide conservation designation does not imply easy comprehensive tourist viewing or 9.5 uniqueness. Source: https://www.wwf.org.kh/about_us/where_we_work/mekong_flooded_forest/

preah-khan-angkor|9.3,9.7,9.7,9.4,9.0|-|Retain substantial sprawling temple dedicated by Jayavarman VII and its historical role; complex has multiple exploration zones, distinguished from Angkor park's broader ensemble. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/12/preah-khan-temple/

preah-vihear-temple|9.5,9.9,9.8,9.3,9.1|-|Retain exceptional 800-metre axial mountaintop Khmer sanctuary and world heritage significance independent of current border conflict; access restricted as of November 2026 and score does not imply open. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1224

prey-lang-wildlife-sanctuary|8.8,9.3,9.0,8.1,8.7|-|Cambodia's major biodiverse lowland forest remains internationally important but is under deforestation pressure; specialized conservation/research visits are not equivalent to a highly developed safari visitor experience. Source: https://cambodia.conservation.org/projects/prey-lang-wildlife-sanctuary

ta-prohm-temple|9.6,9.8,9.7,9.6,8.9|-|Retain rare internationally celebrated interaction of massive tree roots with 12th-century Khmer masonry, a substantial temple in its own right but below Angkor Wat overall. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/12/ta-prohm/

veun-sai-siem-pang-national-park|8.8,9.3,9.0,8.3,8.8|-|Threatened gibbon and primate forest habitat is ecologically exceptional, while community ecotourism is still specialized; reduce near-perfect conventional visitor depth and uniqueness claims. Source: https://cambodia.conservation.org/projects/veun-sai-siem-pang-national-park

prek-toal-bird-sanctuary|8.7,9.1,8.9,8.6,8.3|nature=9.2|The Tonle Sap floodplain breeding grounds host large threatened waterbird colonies with high biological value, but a guided boat visit does not inherit the entire lake's ecology or discovery breadth. Source: https://cambodia.wcs.org/Wildlife/Ibis-Other-Waterbirds/Important-Sites-for-Waterbirds.aspx

phnom-aural|8.8,8.9,8.5,8.5,8.6|nature=9.0,adventure=9.0|Cambodia's tallest mountain is an important local climbing objective, but mountain height within one country does not imply globally singular altitude or visitor depth beside Everest or Yushan. Source: https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/en/site/factsheet/16665

phnom-da-temple|8.5,9.0,9.2,8.6,7.5|architecture=9.0,history=9.2|Significant early Khmer-Funan sacred hill site and sculptural context, although today's comparatively modest surviving temple does not rival Angkor's scale or preservation. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6455/

bakong-temple|8.8,9.1,9.2,8.9,8.0|architecture=9.3,history=9.3|Early Khmer state-temple pyramid remains of outstanding regional importance, but a single temple should not automatically carry 9.5 worldwide architecture and history categories from the full Roluos group. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/03/bakong/

southern-cardamom-national-park|8.9,9.1,8.8,8.5,8.8|nature=9.3,wildlife=9.3|Large tropical forest conservation system supports threatened species, but specialist ranger and guided trekking visits offer less reliable breadth than accessible world-reference national parks. Source: https://www.rainforesttrust.org/urgent-projects/conserving-cardamoms-wildlife/

phnom-bakheng|8.8,9.0,9.3,8.7,7.5|architecture=9.3,history=9.3|Historic Angkor-era temple mountain and valued sunset vantage, yet the contained pilgrimage viewpoint cannot inherit all Angkor's heritage distinction and exploration depth. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/09/phnom-bakheng/

banteay-samre|8.6,9.0,9.1,8.8,7.6|architecture=9.2,history=9.2|Well-preserved Angkor-era sandstone sanctuary shows refined Khmer craftsmanship; comparatively compact grounds and many regional peers argue against 9.5 international uniqueness. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/temples/

oudong-royal-stupas|8.6,9.0,9.2,8.8,7.7|architecture=9.0,history=9.2|Post-Angkor Cambodian royal capital monuments represent meaningful dynastic continuity, but modest surviving complexes should not equal world-defining ancient imperial cities. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6459/

river-of-thousand-lingas|8.6,9.1,9.0,8.8,7.7|history=9.1|Kbal Spean's carved riverbed combines religious art and forest hike, but relatively localized carvings and trail scope differ from Angkor's monumental sanctuary complexes. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/05/kbal-spean/

neak-pean|8.6,9.1,9.0,8.8,7.3|architecture=9.2,photography=9.2|Distinctive island shrine and ceremonial healing pools remain an architectural highlight, while focused site footprint offers far less exploration than an Angkor-scale heritage complex. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/09/neak-pean/

phnom-aural-wildlife-sanctuary|8.8,9.0,8.7,8.3,8.6|nature=9.2|Forest mountain sanctuary preserves substantial habitat and seasonal biodiversity, yet specialized mountain access should not be counted as reliably deep developed visitor exploration. Source: https://data.opendevelopmentcambodia.net/library_record/management-plan-phnom-aural-wildlife-sanctuary-2022-2031

siem-pang-wildlife-sanctuary|8.8,9.1,8.8,8.4,8.6|nature=9.3|Critically endangered ibis and dry forest wildlife justify strong ecological scores, though conservation fieldwork and specialist birding cannot be treated as comparable to multi-site leisure visits. Source: https://iucn.org/story/202604/rewilding-siem-pang-wildlife-sanctuary-cambodia-learning-and-scaling-opportunity-viet

banteay-chhmar-towers|8.8,9.0,9.0,8.6,7.3|architecture=9.2,history=9.2|Noteworthy face towers belong to the wider Banteay Chhmar temple, and a specific tower grouping has less independent historic scope and depth than the complex itself. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6456/

yeak-laom-volcanic-lake|8.5,8.7,7.9,8.8,8.0|nature=9.0|Beautiful crater lake with important local indigenous stewardship and recreation, but volcanic crater lakes are comparatively replaceable worldwide and 9.5 uniqueness is not justified. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/activities/community-based-tourism-cbt/yeak-laom-community-based-ecotourism-site.htm

bokor-national-park|8.6,9.0,8.6,8.9,8.8|-|Forested Bokor highlands, hill-station history and coastal panoramas support a worthwhile park experience; a 9.5 exploration depth was too high relative to vast globally elite tropical landscapes. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/attractions/kampot/bokor-hill-station.htm

kulen-promtep-wildlife-sanctuary|8.8,9.1,8.8,8.3,8.7|-|Important rare bird habitat in northern Cambodia, with giant ibis conservation and community-linked eco-tourism, while narrow specialist access does not establish world-leading conventional visitor experience. Source: https://iucn.org/content/ibises-tmatbauy-village-a-model-bird-conservation-northern-cambodia

peam-krasaop-wildlife-sanctuary|8.6,8.9,8.6,8.7,8.4|nature=9.1,wildlife=9.1|Coastal mangrove habitat with boardwalk visits and estuary wildlife, but the short accessible visitor circuit is not the full extent of Khmer coastal forest ecosystems. Source: https://visitcambodia.info/places/peam-krasaop-wildlife-sanctuary/

west-baray|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.1,7.7|history=9.3|Huge historic Khmer reservoir demonstrates sophisticated Angkor hydraulic engineering, but a waterbody stop is less immersive than the complete urban hydraulic system and associated temples. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/668

boeung-chhmar-reserve|8.6,9.0,8.8,8.5,8.8|nature=9.2,wildlife=9.2|Seasonally flooded Tonle Sap Ramsar area is ecologically important, while specialized birdwatching and boat trips should not automatically receive park-wide maximum visitor depth. Source: https://www.ramsar.org/country-profile/cambodia

phnom-chisor-temple|8.6,8.9,9.0,8.6,7.5|architecture=9.1,history=9.1|Elevated Khmer stone sanctuary has historical landscape interest, but a single hilltop temple and steps have less world-cultural singularity than major Angkor monument groups. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/attractions/takeo/phnom-chisor.htm

bokor-hill-station|8.0,8.2,8.2,8.4,8.0|architecture=8.4,history=8.5|Bokor Hill Station's 1920s French colonial resort buildings, later abandonment and restorations make an interesting Cambodian historic excursion, not a globally rare intact town ensemble. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/news/localnews/23943/preserving-history-on-bokor-hill-station.htm

prasat-sambor|8.6,9.0,9.1,8.7,7.5|architecture=9.1,history=9.2|The northern Prasat Sambor temple group is one part of the larger UNESCO Sambor Prei Kuk archaeological property; important pre-Angkor ruins but not the breadth of the entire Ishanapura site. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1532

banteay-kdei|8.6,9.0,8.9,8.8,7.7|architecture=9.2,history=9.2|Banteay Kdei is a substantial late-Angkor monastic temple noted by APSARA for educational and religious functions, but its narrower historical significance must not duplicate that of Angkor Thom or Angkor Wat. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2026/08/03/banteay-kdei-temple/

mondulkiri-highlands|8.6,8.8,8.1,8.5,9.0|nature=9.0,photography=8.9|Mondulkiri's large rural plateau has forests, waterfalls and indigenous settlements but also fragmented habitats and industrial agriculture, limiting worldwide uniqueness and uniformly immersive visitor depth. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/visit-cambodia/attractions/mondulkiri.htm

ta-keo|8.6,9.1,9.1,8.8,7.7|architecture=9.3,history=9.3|APSARA documents Ta Keo as a remarkable unfinished circa-1000 sandstone temple-mountain with monumental geometric layout; retain impressive architecture but not full Angkor-scale depth. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2026/07/15/discover-the-history-and-unique-features-of-takeo-temple/

prasat-yeai-poeun|8.4,8.8,8.9,8.5,7.4|architecture=9.0,history=9.0|Southern Prasat Yeai Poeun brick temple group has important early Khmer sacred architecture but is one of several distinct component clusters of the Sambor Prei Kuk UNESCO ensemble. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1532

jahoo-gibbon-camp|8.3,9.0,8.6,8.8,7.8|wildlife=9.2|Jahoo Gibbon Camp is a specialist community birding and primate-observation site in eastern Cambodia; sightings and local conservation merit do not imply near-perfect worldwide rarity or broad visitor depth. Source: https://cambodia.conservation.org/

oudong-mountain|8.1,8.6,9.0,8.5,8.1|history=9.1|Oudong's hilltop royal stupas and old capital heritage make a meaningful religious hike, but named mountain stop should not inherit the full history and monument depth of the former Cambodian capital. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/

phnom-banan|8.4,8.9,9.0,8.7,7.6|architecture=9.1,history=9.1|Phnom Banan is a compelling hilltop Khmer sanctuary accessible by stairs, but one compact five-tower temple offers less breadth than the multi-building Angkor archaeological ensembles. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kh

prasat-pram|8.5,8.9,8.7,8.8,7.5|architecture=9.1,photography=9.2|The tree-root-wrapped Prasat Pram temples are photogenic Koh Ker outliers with a comparatively short visit and less historical scope than the entire UNESCO Koh Ker archaeological site. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kh

elephant-valley-project|8.5,8.7,8.6,9.1,8.3|wildlife=9.2|Elephant Valley Project has substantial ethical elephant care, welfare education and conservation programs; strong visitor experience is not automatically rare global landscape uniqueness or all-day natural depth. Source: https://elephantvalleyproject.org/visit-options/

ream-national-park|8.3,8.7,8.0,8.5,8.7|nature=9.0,wildlife=8.9|Ream protects Cambodian coastal forest, mangroves and beaches, yet regional nature value and access pressures should not make every core rating globally outstanding by default. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/

angkor-wat-west-gate|8.4,8.8,8.9,8.5,7.0|architecture=9.2,history=9.1|The west entrance causeway and gateway form an impressive but short individual component of Angkor Wat; they cannot inherit the entire iconic temple's monumental visit depth. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2025/10/16/visiting-angkor-wat-temple/

east-mebon|8.5,8.9,9.0,8.8,7.7|architecture=9.2,history=9.2|East Mebon is a major 10th-century temple originally standing in the East Baray reservoir, but still a specific single temple and not a full UNESCO historical city. Source: https://apsaraauthority.gov.kh/2021/08/05/east-mebon/

kirirom-national-park|8.4,8.8,8.0,8.8,8.6|nature=9.0|Kirirom offers pine forests and cool highland walks, worthwhile regional nature but less globally rare and biologically defining than the extensive Cardamom mountain ecosystems. Source: https://www.tourismcambodia.com/

prasat-tao|8.3,8.9,8.9,8.6,7.4|architecture=9.0,history=9.0|Prasat Tao Lion Temple is a focused carved sanctuary component at Sambor Prei Kuk; rare sculpture merits respect but does not confer full global ensemble depth on one monument. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1532

ang-trapeang-thmor|8.8,9.2,9.2,8.4,8.7|-|Ang Trapeang Thmor is a protected Cambodian wetland and important winter habitat for endangered Sarus cranes; exceptional conservation merits do not guarantee a globally elite conventional tourist visit or wide hiking depth. Source: https://cambodia.wcs.org/Wildlife/Sarus-Crane/Conservation-at-Ang-Trapeang-Thmor.aspx

former-m13-prison-site|8.7,9.2,9.9,8.7,7.7|-|Former M-13 prison is a distinct component of Cambodia's 2025 UNESCO-listed Khmer Rouge memorial sites, with profound historic significance and comparatively modest standalone ruin/interpretation breadth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1748/

areng-valley|8.9,9.2,8.8,8.6,9.1|-|Areng Valley contains rainforest and traditional community-managed ecotourism within the Southern Cardamom landscape, offering serious nature excursions while not equal to the entire protected mountain range's world-scale ecology. Source: https://www.areng-valley.org/

ta-som|8.6,9.0,9.1,8.7,7.7|-|Ta Som is a compact Angkor-period temple and famous tree-rooted eastern gate within the much larger Angkor Archaeological Park; its photo appeal is strong but the temple cannot inherit the park's UNESCO-scale archaeological depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/668

terrace-of-the-leper-king|8.5,9.0,9.1,8.6,7.2|-|Terrace of the Leper King preserves impressive layered carved stone walls at Angkor Thom, but is a short terrace monument stop rather than an entire religious or urban archaeological ensemble. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/668

lumphat-wildlife-sanctuary|8.8,9.1,9.1,8.0,8.6|-|Lumphat Wildlife Sanctuary supports rare eastern Cambodian dry forest and threatened wildlife, but limited visitor access and specialist birding reduce conventional tour experience relative to the region's ecological importance. Source: https://www.iucn.org/our-work/region/asia/cambodia
